payload.summary: Wrote STORAGE.md at the workspace root. Recommends one-file-per-note (UTF-8 Markdown + front matter, date-sharded under notes/YYYY/MM/) as the source of truth, plus a derived, disposable SQLite FTS5 index; governing rule is 'note files are truth, index is derived and disposable'. Covers all three constraints: FTS5 inverted-index search with order-of-magnitude scale arithmetic at ~50k notes and a runtime FTS5 availability probe with scan-based fallback; crash safety via the complete durable-write sequence (same-directory mkstemp -> flush -> os.fsync -> os.replace -> POSIX parent-directory fsync), explicitly distinguishing SIGKILL (satisfied by temp+rename alone, since page-cache data survives process death) from power loss (needs fsync); and hand-readability via plain Markdown files usable with cat/grep/git. Documents three rejected alternatives with reasons tied to the Python 3 / single-user / single-machine / no-concurrent-writers context: SQLite-as-source-of-truth (opaque binary, no meaningful diffs, total-loss blast radius with no replica or ops team), append-only JSONL with compaction (newline-escaped bodies defeat hand-readability, O(total history) queries including deleted notes, whole-store rewrite at compaction, and the append-only shape solves a multi-writer problem jot does not have), and one-file-per-note with no index (seconds-long scans at 50k files, no ranking or stemming, rg would be a hard external dependency on Windows) - the last explicitly framed as distinct from the recommendation and retained as the FTS5-absent fallback. Trade-offs section leads with the index-drift window including the phantom-delete case, plus its mtime/size detection and self-heal path and jot reindex escape hatch, then O(n) reindex cost, dual-representation code surface, per-file inode/block overhead, slow tree copies, and the owned front-matter parsing surface. Docs-only ticket: no CLI code written, no other board files touched.
